title: POC HealthTech data lifecycle & DPA options
content:
Context:
This is a working notes doc for the HealthTech POC kicked off 2025-02-10. Customer is a mid-size digital health provider (clinical decision support + patient messaging) evaluating Redwood Inference for both hosted and private deployment options. Primary ask: how we handle PHI-like data, retention windows, auditability, and a minimal DPA addendum they can present to their security/legal teams.

High-level goals for this doc (working):
- Capture realistic data flows for the demo POC and a production ramp scenario.
- Enumerate pragmatic DPA addendum options we can offer (short list for legal).
- Outline retention/ephemeral defaults + optional stricter controls for HealthTech customers.
- Surface operational/engineering implications and quick implementation checklist for the POC.

Quick summary / recommendation (first pass):
- For the POC: use Hosted API with request-level ephemeral-mode + strict session KV cache TTL = 0 (no persistent logs of request/response), enable customer-provided KMS for encryption-at-rest, and ship audit logs to their syslog (S3) with redaction.
- For production (if PHI required): recommend Private deployment (VPC) or Dedicated with contractual DPA addendum specifying no-logs mode, 30-day retention max for aggregated telemetry, mandatory KMS integration, and quarterly privacy attestation reports.

Data inventory (POC demo flows) - preliminary list:
- Input examples: free-text patient symptoms (PHI-ish), structured patient id (hashed), clinician notes, timestamps.
- Outputs: suggested next steps, risk score scalar, truncated clinician-facing summary.
- Derived telemetry: latency, token usage, error traces, prompt hash.
- Retention candidates: raw requests, raw responses, prompt templates, debug traces.

Customer constraints to respect:
- No persistent storage of raw PHI outside customer-controlled S3 buckets.
- Audit trail required for every training/feedback export event.
- Encryption keys must be customer-managed (KMS/HSM) for production.
- Regulatory preference: mirror of logs to their SIEM for 1 year, but Redwood should not retain raw PHI longer than 30 days unless explicitly agreed.

POC options (3 variants) - pros/cons and engineering notes:
1) Ephemeral-hosted (fastest demo)
   - What: Hosted API + ephemeral-mode flag; Redwood keeps only aggregated telemetry; raw request/response persisted only if customer enables opt-in storage; default TTL=0.
   - Pros: fastest onboarding, no infra handoff, we can demo features quickly.
   - Cons: customer legal might reject hosted handling of any PHI. Need explicit contract language.
   - Eng notes: enable request.redact=true in demo account; route audit logs to customer S3 via signed URL; ensure no prompt caching.

2) Hosted-with-cust-s3 (mid)
   - What: Hosted API but raw payloads archived to customer-managed S3/GCS with enforced lifecycle rules. Redwood retains only pointers.
   - Pros: meets customers who want control of raw data; lower ops friction vs full private.
   - Cons: slightly more integration work, still involves network egress from Redwood infra.
   - Eng notes: implement sign-in-once S3 write policy, provide ingestion lambda example for redaction, document lifecycle policy snippet.

3) Private / VPC deployment (production-grade)
   - What: Private control plane + on-prem or VPC compute; full data locality, KMS/HSM-integration, audit logs kept in-customer environment.
   - Pros: best for regulated PHI workloads, supports strict SLAs and isolation.
   - Cons: longer lead time, infra + SRE support cost, contractual commitments.
   - Eng notes: prep playbook for private deployment checklist (network peering, subnet sizing, certificate rotation, KMS key provisioning).

Suggested DPA addendum language (short snippets for legal to consider) - draft, informal:
- Data classification: Redwood will treat requests and responses from the customer’s POC environment as Customer Data. Redwood will not access or use Customer Data for model training or improvement unless explicitly authorized in writing.
- No-logs option: For POC accounts marked as NO_LOGS, Redwood shall not persist raw request or response payloads beyond 48 hours except as required for debug with prior customer approval.
- Encryption: All persisted Customer Data will be encrypted at rest using customer-provided keys (KMS) where available; communications will be TLS 1.2+ with mutual TLS optional for Private deployments.
- Auditability: Redwood will provide access to detailed audit logs (access, request metadata, routing decisions) via a customer-specified S3 bucket or syslog endpoint; raw payloads will be subject to the No-logs clause.
- Subprocessors: Redwood will provide a current list of subprocessors and notify customer 30 days before any changes that affect data residency.

Retention/TTL proposal table (text) - baseline for negotiation:
- Raw requests/responses: POC default = delete within 48 hours (opt-in store for customer-managed archival).
- Prompt cache / KV: default TTL = 0 for HealthTech POC; production may use TTL up to 7 days if encrypted and customer-consented.
- Aggregated telemetry (non-PII): 365 days by default for billing/monitoring; can be shortened on request.
- Audit logs (metadata only): 1 year mirrored to customer SIEM; Redwood retention of metadata only 90 days.

Operational checklist for running the POC (engineering + SE tasks):
- [ ] Create demo tenant flagged as NO_LOGS and ephemeral-mode enabled.
- [ ] Provide the customer a signed S3 write URL and example ingestion lambda (redaction sample).
- [ ] Configure KMS integration (test key) and verify encryption-at-rest for any persisted artifacts.
- [ ] Instrument prompts to emit prompt-hashes not raw text when storing telemetry.
- [ ] Confirm network egress path and document packet flow for customer's security team.
- [ ] Run a privacy workshop with customer security/legal on 2025-02-20 (agenda draft below).

Workshop draft agenda (30–45 min)
- Introductions (5)
- POC goals & data flows (10)
- Technical demo: ephemeral-mode + S3 export (10)
- Legal/controls discussion: proposed DPA snippets + retention table (10)
- Next steps and decision gates (5)

Open questions / risks to resolve:
- Customer insists on zero retention of any raw request anywhere — can we offer guaranteed never-stored path for hosted? (short answer: yes if ephemeral-mode + stream-only and we disable on-call debug storage, but must add contractual clause and engineering guardrails).
- Does the customer require model-explainability artifacts that contain prompt text? If yes, we need a redaction layer and a policy for what gets stored for explainability.
- Subprocessor list acceptance timeline — legal may request SOC2 + updated list before POC start.

Example clause for "never store PHI" (developer-friendly) - raw text to hand to legal:
"Redwood will process Customer Data solely to provide the Services and will not persist raw request or response payloads originating from the Customer’s POC tenant beyond 48 hours, except with Customer’s written authorization. For the avoidance of doubt, Customer Data will not be used for model training or augmentation without explicit permission. Redwood will implement technical controls to prevent developer-facing backups from containing Customer Data."

Notes to SEs (implementation tips)
- Use streaming output for demo so we do not need to buffer full responses server-side.
- Flag telemetry with prompt-hash instead of plaintext. Make the hash algorithm and salt deterministic per-tenant to avoid cross-tenant correlation.
- When enabling customer S3 export, provide a small validation utility that uploads a checksum file so the customer can verify writes.

Next steps (short-term):
- Finalize the DPA snippets with Legal (owner: Priya) by 2025-02-18.
- Run technical dry-run of NO_LOGS demo by 2025-02-20 (owner: Jordan).
- Send a 1-page slide that maps each POC option to customer compliance requirements (owner: Ava) by 2025-02-16.

Appendix — quick trace of POC request path (text):
Client -> Redwood API Gateway (edge) -> Authz check -> Routing policy (ephemeral/no-store) -> Inference runtime (no persistent KV) -> Stream to client + optional one-way S3 write to customer bucket (signed). Audit events (metadata-only) emitted to shared logging pipeline and mirrored to customer SIEM.

End notes: this doc intentionally informal — will convert to a polished DPA addendum draft once legal has accepted core language. Keep comments/edits inline and flag anything that needs redaction before sharing with customer.

Action items (inline):
- Priya: legal-first pass on clauses + subprocessors list (due 2025-02-18)
- Jordan: engineering dry-run (due 2025-02-20)
- Ava: customer slide + S3 lambda sample (due 2025-02-16)

-- Ava M.
